messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: Rhmr managing retries / skip
messages.body_plain:
You have two options.

If you are using 0.72

a) rhwatch(..., debug='count')

this will capture all such errors and report them through hadoop counters. It wont kill the job.
This will trap /all/ errors thus the ones you want to ignore and the ones you dont want to ignore.

b) Or wrap the offending code in tryCatch. Suppose Foo is the offending function/expression called

tryCatch({
  code1
  foo()
}, error=function(e) {
   rhcounter("MY_ERRORS",as.character(e), 1)
})

This will stop your job from failing.

Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] rhmr copyFiles parameter
messages.body_plain:
What this does is:

if in the R code you create a file and save it in "./tmp/", and copyFiles is TRUE, then all these files will be copied to the job output folder.

e.g.

map = expression({
for(a in map.values) {
  pdf(sprintf("tmp/%s.pdf",taskid))
  plot(runif(100))
dev.off()
}
}

And copyfiles=TRUE, then at end of job there will be many pdf files ...

messages.subject: Beta test 0.73
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Should you choose to, you may beta test 0.73

https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/blob/unstable/code/Rhipe_0.73.tar.gz?raw=true

I am using this daily, so your bugs will be fixed quickly :)

Cheers
Saptarshi

Note, rhwrite has changed in 0.73. See ?rhwrite

One nice feature for testing: rhJobInfo which takes the job id returns the timing information of all the tasks.
0.73 has improved MapFile performance and rhread is much faster.

If you have comments about the R help pages, send recommendations. They will be incorporated.
This is currently in the 'unstable' branch but hopefully by end of Feb, middle March it will be stable.

0.74 will remove the custom R binary and will be entirely in rJava, JRI and some C code. Installation should hopefully be simpler, though you'll still need to compile with protobuf!

Cheers
Saptarshi

I am using rHipe map reduce to perform linear regression in my mapper. It takes in a directory and runs regression on each file. However, each file has a different number of columns (ie. different number of x variables).

I know the way to call the linear regression function is lm(y~ x1 + x2 + x3... +xn), and I am able to generate dynamically N number of xn columns and assign them to the correct column in the file. My question is, how can I dynamically call the lm() function with my different xn variables?

ie.

lm (y~x1+x2+x3)
lm (y~x1+x2+x3+x4+x5)
lm (y~x1)
...

thanks so much in advance!

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] rhsave / rhwrite within mapper
messages.body_plain:
Inside a RHIPE job, rhsave will not work.

Why not use rhcollect? do this
a <- lm(...)
rhcollect(somekey, serialize(a, NULL) )

You need to serialize lm objects because these contains R classes that RHIPE's native serializer does not know how to handle.

When you read the data back in say through rhread

y=rhread(outputfolder)
key = y[[1]] [[1]]
lm.object = unserialize(y[[1]][[2]])

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Rhipe 0.72 Error
messages.body_plain:
Hmm,

rhwatch uses input and output for input folders and output folders. See ?rhwatch
also, see rhfmt for specifying the input to 'input'. By default

input="path to something" assumes sequence file input format.
If you want text input  fornat, you need input=rhfmt(path-to-input, type='text')

see rhoptions()$ioformats$text for what options you can pass.

Regards
Saptarshi

messages.body_plain:
This will not work. You input folder is Rdata files? What you're thinking of MultilFileInputFormat which
RHIPE does not support (maybe in future).

I recommend you upgrade to 0.72.1

You have two options,
a) use rhls(input folder) to see how many rdata files you have, say L
then rhwatch(, input=c(L, K))

K is a level of parallelism.

Each mapper will get a number from 1 to L. Use system("hadoop dfs -get path-to-i'thRdata file ./")
and then do load("ith Rdata file"). So map.values will be a  subset of 1 to L

b) instead of saving Rdata via rhsave, save your text files to the HDFS using rhcollect(someindex, data). Of course you probably still
have many text files? Then each file will be one map task. Save the entire file (like you're doing) and instead write using rhcollect(filename, data)
using sequence as the output format.

and use 0.72.1. 0.69 wont be supported.
https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/blob/master/code/Rhipe_0.72.1.tar.gz?raw=true

Thank you for your prompt reply....I guess I am okay with just loading 1 file a time now. Is there not an easy way to rhsave an R Object and then re-load it back to the mapper?

I was taking a look at this: https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/blob/master/contributed/unit_test/unit_test.export.rdata.sim.data.R

This is my code now. Could you tell me what is wrong? thanks so much again.

======================================
rhinit(TRUE, TRUE, buglevel=2000)

args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)

input_dest <- args[1]
ouput_dest <- args[2]

data <- replicate(6,rnorm(6))
rhsave("data",file = "/user/xxxx/test2.RData",envir=environment() )

############################################

map.setup = expression ({
load("test2.RData")
})

map <- expression({
fname <- Sys.getenv("mapred.input.file") # get name of file being processed
raw <- map.values
nvars <- length(raw[,1])

rhcollect(fname, nvars) # nvars should be 6
})

mr_result <- rhmr(map=map,reduce=NULL, inout=c("text", "text"), mapred=list(mapred.reduce.tasks=0)
        ,ifolder=input_dest, shared="/user/xxxx/test2.RData"
        ,ofolder=ouput_dest)

job.result <- rhstatus(rhex(mr_result,async=FALSE),mon.sec=2)

if(job.result$state != "SUCCEEDED") {
  print("JOB FAILED")
} else
print("JOB COMPLETE SUCCESSFULLY")
